item.title: The toolkit
item.description:
go-widgets/toolkit is the widget set. Every widget implements the same interface — Bounds, SetBounds,Draw(p painter.Painter, theme *Theme), HitTest, OnEvent — so a host treats a button, a table and an event calendar alike. Standard library only,CGO_ENABLED=0, 100% statement coverage.

At v0.329.0 it has 160 exported widget types in about 69,000 lines of widget code. Those two numbers are measured at that tag, not carried over: the toolkit’s README gives the commands, and they should be run again rather than the figures repeated.

The families

Family Widgets
Action Button, ToggleButton, CheckButton, RadioButton + RadioGroup, Switch, SplitButton, IconButton, CycleButton, Chip, SegmentedBar
Input Entry, TextView (selection, IME preview, syntax spans, line numbers), SpinButton, Scale, RangeSlider, SearchEntry, TagField, ComboBox, FormField with Validate/Rule
Selection ListBox, TreeView, DropDown
Containers Container with a swappable Layout (FitLayout, BoxLayout, BorderLayout, CardLayout, FlowLayout); HBox, VBox, Grid, Frame, Dock, Border, Stack, Overlay, Paned, Splitter, Expander, Accordion; a declarative Node builder
Navigation Menu, MenuBar (with Alt+letter), ContextMenu, Popover, CommandPalette, Dialog, MessageDialog, Wizard, Notebook, ViewSwitcher, Carousel
Feedback ProgressBar, ProgressCircle, LevelBar, Spinner, Tooltip, Notification, Toast, Banner, Alert, Badge, Skeleton
Data Table (cell editing, frozen columns, group rows, aggregates, row expanders), TreeTable, PropertyGrid, Kanban, Gantt, Agenda (week, month, quarter, year; several calendars)
Charts LineChart, BarChart, PieChart, AreaChart, ScatterChart, RadarChart, Gauge, Sparkline
Composite FileChooser, FileTree, ColorChooser, ColorPicker, FontChooser, Calendar, DatePicker, DateRangePicker, TimePicker, MarkdownView, MarkdownEditor, TerminalView
Shell Window with client-side decorations, HeaderBar, Toolbar, Ribbon, Statusbar, StatusIcon, StatusArea, Wallpaper, Thumbnail

Every one of them, live: the gallery.

Ribbon

Ribbon is an Office-style command ribbon: tabs of labelled groups holding large buttons (icon above the text), small ones (icon beside it), toggles, split buttons, drop-downs and a small gallery. It follows the Windows ribbon guidelines: as the window narrows each group steps down by priority — full,compact, icons only, then one pop-up button — so the ribbon shows the largest combination that fits; it collapses to its tabs (Ctrl+F1, or the chevron) and a tab then peeks at its body; Alt shows keytips; tooltips carry the shortcut and a description. Tab and toolbar navigation follow the WAI-ARIA patterns, and its boundaries and focus ring keep 3:1 contrast in light and dark themes.

Every control is a view on an Action — the one command a menu, a palette and the ribbon share — and NewCommandAction makes one from a view-modelmvvm.Command, so its CanExecute greys the control. The active tab, the collapsed state, a toggle and a drop-down’s choice are mvvm.Observables. Put the ribbon under a PopoverHost and its menus draw over the page with no host code.

RibbonGrid is a control kind whose pop-up is a GridCols by GridRows grid of cells (8 by 6 when zero, at most 16 by 16), as the Table button of a word processor has. The pointer or the arrow keys light the cells from the corner up to the one under them and a caption says “3 × 2”; a click or Enter chooses and calls OnGrid(cols, rows); Home and End jump, Escape closes. It is drawn in light and dark and reported to assistive technology as a button that is expanded while the grid is open.

&toolkit.RibbonControl{Kind: toolkit.RibbonGrid, Label: "Table",
 GridCols: 8, GridRows: 8,
 OnGrid: insertTable}

Splitter

Splitter lays N panes side by side (or one above the other, withvertical true) and puts a draggable, focusable divider between each neighbouring pair, after the WAI-ARIA window-splitter pattern. A pane is either fixed — its Size, in logical pixels, is an mvvm.Observable[int] the divider writes — or flexible, sharing what the fixed panes leave by itsWeight, also an Observable. Each pane has a Min and a Max. ACollapsible fixed pane closes (size 0) when the divider is pulled below half its Min, or on a double-click or Enter, and opens again the same way. A pane’sVisible observable switches it and its divider off. Because the sizes live in observables, a view-model can bind, persist and restore them; OnResized is called once per finished gesture with the panes the person changed, never for a layout that merely followed a window resize.

files := mvvm.NewObservable(240) // fixed pane, logical px
w := mvvm.NewObservable(1) // flexible pane, weight

s := toolkit.NewSplitter(false,
 &toolkit.SplitPane{Widget: tree, Name: "Files", Size: files,
 Min: 120, Max: 480, Collapsible: true},
 &toolkit.SplitPane{Widget: editor, Name: "Editor", Weight: w, Min: 200},
)
s.OnResized = func(changed []int) { save(files.Get(), w.Get()) }

A divider takes the focus: the arrow keys (Up and Down when vertical) move it by Step logical pixels, four times that with Shift; Home and End take the pane before it to its smallest and largest; Enter collapses or restores the fixed pane it controls; Tab moves between dividers. Each divider is aRoleSeparator with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow, named“Resize” and the pane’s Name. Cursor(x, y) returns "col-resize" or"row-resize" over a divider, and SplitterColors(theme) gives the divider line and accent, which keep 3:1 contrast against the background and surface in both default themes, as the focus ring does.

Themes

One Theme value cascades through the whole tree: change a colour at the root and every widget repaints with it. DefaultLight() and DefaultDark() are built in, and LoadGTKTheme(css) reads the @define-color block of any GTK 3 or libadwaita theme — Adwaita, WhiteSur, Solarized — into a Theme.

Text

The compiled-in default is a 5×7 bitmap font, so pixel tests keep their geometry. One call switches the whole UI to anti-aliased, shaped text:

toolkit.UseOpenTypeText() // Atkinson Hyperlegible, bundled; js/wasm-safe

The face comes from go-opentype/fonts and is rasterised by go-opentype,in Go, with no C font library and no system font lookup.NewTrueTypeFont(ttf, px) loads another face; NewFallbackFont chains several, for example to add a CJK or Arabic face; a widget’s own Font field overrides the global one for that widget alone.

Input

Mouse, keyboard, IME composition, touch (EventTouchStart/Move/End, withGestureRecognizer for taps, long presses and swipes), drag and drop(DragSource, DropTarget). Multi-row selection in ListBox, Table andTreeView works from the mouse and from the keyboard, and honours ⌘ as well as Ctrl, because on macOS Ctrl-click is the secondary click.

Several people in one buffer

collabui.CollabText binds a CodeEditor to one text part of ago-crdt/collab session. The merge is the CRDT’s and the binding adds none of it. Where an edit is applied is the binding’s, and that is a different question.

A peer’s edit merges into the replica the moment it arrives off the wire; the editor is repainted later, when the host runs the closure the binding handed it. In between, the screen shows one text and the replica holds another — and a keystroke in that window was aimed at the screen. Applied at its raw offset it lands elsewhere, and every replica agrees on the result, which is why it does not look like a defect. It was one:

the person did before now
typed Y after the abc on screen, while Xabc had merged XabYc XabcY
deleted the bc on screen, a peer’s X between them acd — the peer’s X destroyed aXd

A local edit is carried across that gap before it is applied: the inclusion transformation of Ellis & Gibbs (SIGMOD ‘89), on the side Jupiter (Nichols et al., UIST ‘95) transforms on — our own edit against what has already merged.An offset moves with what landed before it and goes the same distance into what replaced it. A deletion takes the characters the person could see and not the ones they could not, so a peer’s insertion inside the deleted range is deletedaround and survives. Placement is a guess; a character that was on somebody’s screen a moment ago is not.

Binary size: a program links what it uses

The toolkit is one large package, and that is fine for the linker: Go’s dead-code elimination keeps only what is reachable from main.main and from the init tasks of every imported package. Widgets a program never touches are dropped. What is not dropped is anything a package-level initializer or an imported package’s init reaches, so since v0.345.0 the toolkit keeps its own initializers empty of work and avoids importing packages whose init drags code in:

  • Material and Thumbnail use the codec-freegithub.com/go-images/images/ops,not github.com/go-images/images, whose decoders register themselves ininit (about 1.7 MB of WebAssembly code).
  • CollabText, NewCollabText, MetaName and MetaColor moved togithub.com/go-widgets/toolkit/collabui: they need a livego-crdt/collab session, whose transports pull net/http and crypto/tls.CollabSheet and IsoCRDTDocument need only go-crdt/crdt and stay intoolkit.
  • The e-mail Rule’s regexp, the built-in iso icon registry and theRichEditorToolbar button table are built the first time they are used, not by initializers.

⛔ The move is a breaking change, with no deprecated forwarder. Change the import of the four names above to collabui; nothing else changes.

Sizes for GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm with -ldflags="-s -w", raw and gzip -9:

Program before (raw / gzip) after (raw / gzip)
one Label (v0.345.0) 10.49 / 2.88 MB 7.48 / 2.13 MB
one Label (v0.345.1) 10.49 / 2.88 MB 5.66 / 1.61 MB
go-wasmcontainers/dashboard 20.42 / 5.17 MB 17.72 / 4.58 MB
the relay flow map 22.62 / 5.44 MB 19.95 / 4.85 MB

What remains is mostly the runtime and the OpenType stack the text renderer needs. To see what keeps a symbol in your own program, build with-ldflags=-dumpdep and follow the first-parent chain from the symbol back tomain.main or go:main.inittasks.

v0.345.0 also adds ColorHex and ParseColorHex, to write a colour as hex and read it back.

Accessibility

A toolkit that paints its own pixels gives a screen reader nothing to read unless it says what it drew. Widgets implement Accessible — a role, a name,a value — and CollectA11y gathers them for the host to publish: AT-SPI on Linux through window, and a virtual view hierarchy on Android.

Since v0.359.0, A11yInfo also carries Focused, Disabled, ReadOnly andMultiline. Each A11yNode.Key is a stable path of @<A11yID> or<Type>#<n> segments, with ~2 appended on a duplicate ID, so a host can recognise a node from one frame to the next. A widget may implement the new optional interface A11yIdentified to supply its own ID, and TextView,CodeEditor and Entry have an AccessibleName.

Focus

⛔ Breaking in v0.357.0: Focused() is now HasFocus() on TextView,AddressBar and RichEditor. Migrate with one rename: ed.Focused() becomesed.HasFocus(). Each of the three now implements Focusable, so Tab reaches the editors; CodeEditor inherits this.

Sizing an editor to its content

Since v0.360.0, a TextView or CodeEditor with NoVerticalScroll set lays out every line and never scrolls vertically; long lines still scroll horizontally, and the caret, selection and input methods work as before.PreferredHeight() is an Observable of the height that shows every line: the top inset, the lines, the bottom padding, and the horizontal bar when a line overflows. It changes on edits, undo, a new font or a new width, so a host subscribes once and sizes the surface from the callback, as a notebook does for each code cell.

A file tree over a versioned working tree

FileTree is an Explorer over a flat list of paths: folders first, rename in place with F2, new file and new folder, Delete after a confirmation, a row dragged onto a folder to move it, files dropped from outside, a context menu,the WAI-ARIA treeview keys and type-ahead. It never changes its own entries —every verb becomes a FileRequest handed to OnRequest, and the host applies it and sets Entries, so the store stays the one source of truth.

Since v0.361.0, each FileEntry also carries a Status:

FileStatus mark
FileUnchanged (the zero value) none
FileModified M
FileAdded A
FileDeleted D
FileUntracked ?
FileConflicted !

It is deliberately not “git status”. Those six states are the vocabulary git, Mercurial, Subversion, Jujutsu and Fossil all share, so the tree knows which mark to draw and the host knows why; nothing here understands a commit.The marks are the ones git status --short, hg status and svn status use,and they are drawn inboard of the size, so ShowSizes does not move them.

The meaning is carried by the glyph, not the colour: each status offers two candidate inks and the first that clears 4.5:1 against the row wins, otherwise the row’s own ink is used — so a mark is never unreadable, and a reader who cannot distinguish colours loses nothing. The selected entry’s state is also spoken through A11y, as "main.tex, modified", because a glyph in a colour is unavailable to a screen reader.

A folder’s status is not derived from its children: “a folder holding a modified file” is a policy rather than a fact, and git says nothing about folders at all. An explicit Dir entry carries its own status — a submodule, a directory a merge left conflicted — while an implied parent has none.

Filling the marks from a repository

Since v0.363.0, SetRepository(vcs.Repository) fills the marks from avcs repository, so a host does not set each Status by hand. The toolkit imports only vcs (standard library only),never a driver: the host registers one. The git driver is the separate modulevcs/git (go-git, never the git binary); vcs.Detect(dir) walks up to the nearest repository once a driver is imported.

import (
 "context"

 "github.com/go-widgets/toolkit"
 "github.com/go-widgets/vcs"
 _ "github.com/go-widgets/vcs/git" // registers the "git" driver
)

// newTree shows dir's files with their git state. post hands a closure to the
// host's UI goroutine.
func newTree(dir string, entries []toolkit.FileEntry, post func(func())) (*toolkit.FileTree, error) {
 repo, err := vcs.Detect(dir) // walks up to the nearest repository
 if err != nil {
 return nil, err // vcs.ErrNoRepository when there is none
 }
 tree := toolkit.NewFileTree(entries)
 tree.PostUI = post // Status runs off the UI goroutine
 tree.SetRepository(repo)
 tree.StatusError().Subscribe(func(err error) { /* show it */ })
 return tree, nil
}

// After a change the tree was not told of, say a save:
func saved(tree *toolkit.FileTree) { tree.RefreshStatusAsync() }

// A refresh you can wait for, on a worker or in a test:
func wait(tree *toolkit.FileTree) error { return tree.RefreshStatus(context.Background()) }

How the repository’s states become marks:

  • Modified, Added, Deleted, Untracked and Conflicted map to theFileStatus of the same name. Renamed is FileAdded at the new path.Ignored has no mark, because FileIgnored would draw as nothing.
  • A folder is FileModified when anything under it has a mark, andFileConflicted when anything under it is conflicted (conflicts win). This is the policy the paragraph above declines to guess; attaching a repository is the opt-in. A folder the repository reports itself (a submodule) keeps its state, unless a conflict lies beneath it. A Status a host set on an entry wins over the repository’s.
  • A deleted file is marked only if the host still lists it: the tree invents no rows.
  • Marks() is an Observable of every mark, folders included, for a legend or a“3 changes” badge; StatusError() is the last refresh’s error. A failed refresh keeps the previous marks.

The tree never applies a create, rename, delete, move or import: the host does,and sets Entries, and that Set refreshes the marks. RefreshStatus(ctx) asks now and returns when the marks are applied.

Why PostUI (v0.364.0). Repository.Status can take seconds on a large repository(go-git builds the whole status in memory and takes no context), so it must not run on the UI goroutine, and in a browser it would block the page’s event loop.Set PostUI and every refresh the tree starts (SetRepository, a change ofEntries, RefreshStatusAsync) runs Status on a goroutine of its own and hands the result back as a closure that the host runs on its UI goroutine —the same contract as collabui.CollabText. A newer refresh cancels the one in flight and makes its late answer a no-op, so a slow answer never overwrites a newer one. Without PostUI every refresh is synchronous, which is right for a test or a small tree.
